name: @thetis/tools-files
description: Bounded, path-contained file tools: read, edit, write, search, find and list, each returning token-bounded output with a clear footer.

tools.name: read_path
tools.description: Read a text file as numbered lines, windowed by an offset and a line/byte limit. Use it whenever you need to see the contents of a file inside home or shared, including large ones you'll page through. Precondition: the file must exist, be text (no NUL in the first 8 KiB), and be under 4 MiB. Returns the numbered lines plus a footer stating the range shown and whether more remains; prefer this over cat, sed -n, grep, find or heredocs in exec: it costs fewer tokens, it is bounded, and it tells you when the answer is partial.

path.description: File path, relative to home unless absolute.

limit.description: Max lines to show. Default 400, max 2000.

tools.name: edit_path
tools.description: Replace an exact block of text in a file with new text, writing atomically. Use it for targeted edits once you know the exact old text, rather than rewriting the whole file. Precondition: old_text must appear in the file exactly as given (read the file first to match whitespace), and must be unique unless replace_all is set. Returns a confirmation naming the line and a numbered snippet around the change; prefer this over sed -i or heredocs in exec: it costs fewer tokens, it is bounded, and it tells you when the match was ambiguous or missing.

path.description: File path, relative to home unless absolute.

old_text.description: Exact text to find; must be non-empty.

new_text.description: Text to put in its place.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring uniqueness. Default false.

tools.name: write_path
tools.description: Create a new file, or replace an existing one when overwrite is set, writing atomically. Use it for whole-file creation, not incremental edits. Precondition: parent directories are created automatically, but an existing file is refused unless overwrite is true, so you don't clobber something by accident. Returns a one-line confirmation with the line and byte counts written; prefer this over shell redirection or heredocs in exec: it is bounded and it makes the overwrite decision explicit.

path.description: File path, relative to home unless absolute.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file. Default false.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search a directory tree for lines, files, or a count matching a regular expression. Use it to find where something occurs across many files, instead of reading each one. Precondition: the pattern must be a valid JavaScript regex source; the scan skips .git, node_modules, dist, target, .cache, tool-output and binary files, and stops after 20000 files or the max_results cap. Returns matching lines or files plus a tally line, and says plainly when the result is partial; prefer this over grep or find in exec: it costs fewer tokens, it is bounded, and it tells you when the answer is partial.

path.description: Directory or file to search. Default home.

glob.description: File name glob, e.g. '*.js'. Default all files.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find files by a name glob across a directory tree, newest modification first. Use it to locate files when you know (part of) the name but not the path, instead of a shell find. Precondition: glob is required and, with no '/', matches the file name anywhere in the tree; the same skip list and 20000-file scan bound as search_files applies. Returns matching paths plus a count, noting when only the newest results are shown; prefer this over find in exec: it costs fewer tokens, it is bounded, and it tells you when the answer is partial.

path.description: Directory to search under. Default home.

tools.name: get_directory
tools.description: List a directory's entries, directories first, with file sizes, optionally recursing a few levels deep. Use it to orient yourself in a tree before reading or searching specific files. Precondition: path must be an existing directory; below the top level the same skip list as search_files applies, and depth is capped at 3. Returns the listing bounded at 500 entries with a note when more exist; prefer this over ls -R or find in exec: it costs fewer tokens and it is bounded.

depth.description: How many levels deep to recurse. Default 1, max 3.
